sections.label: GOF withdrawal and healthcare inflation
sections.summary: The GOF was withdrawn in 2007 after anti-competitive concerns, with average annual healthcare inflation of 2.4% before and 2.6% after, falling to about 1.2% between 2013 and 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: It withdrew the GOF in 2007 after it was informed by the Competition Commission of Singapore of anti-competitive concerns.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: There was no significant change in the average annual healthcare inflation rate in the decade preceding and following the 2007 withdrawal of SMA's GOF, which were 2.4% and 2.6% respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Recent policy measures, such as the Pioneer Generation package, MediShield Life subsidies and the Community Health Assist Scheme, have helped to reduce the healthcare inflation rate to about 1.2% between 2013 and 2016.

sections.label: Fee benchmarks and competition
sections.summary: Fee benchmarks will be set by the Ministry with advice from an independent committee of stakeholders, and do not restrict doctors from charging lower or higher fees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The fee benchmarks will be set by the Ministry with advice from an independent committee that comprises stakeholders representing the medical community, providers, patients and payors from both the private and public sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The fee benchmarks are not intended to restrict competition as doctors are not prohibited from charging lower or higher fees if they wish to.

sections.label: Insurers using benchmarks and representation
sections.summary: The Ministry was asked what it would do to prevent insurers from using benchmarks to reduce payouts or reject legitimate claims, and it said all stakeholders should be represented.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: Third, what would the Ministry do to prevent insurers from using the benchmarks to reduce the payouts or to reject legitimate claims?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I think it is important for us, when we do the fee benchmarks, to have representation from all stakeholders – the professionals, the professional bodies and, of course, from patients, consumers.

sections.label: Benchmarks identifying doctors who overcharge
sections.summary: The benchmarks would help identify the small number of doctors who overcharge, giving information to patients, insurers and authorities including the Singapore Medical Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I certainly hope that would not be the case because I believe that the large majority of our doctors have their patients' well-being and concern at the foremost, and that is what they want to focus on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But, of course, the benchmarks would help us to identify the small number of doctors who overcharge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This is information for us to be able to use, for patients to use, for insurers to use and for the authorities, including the Singapore Medical Council, for them to be able to take action and prevent the small number from raising healthcare costs for everyone else.

sections.label: Representing patient groups and consumers
sections.summary: It is not possible to represent every individual, but input and perspective from patient groups and consumers can be part of the process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It would not be possible to represent every single individual, as I am sure Assoc Prof Goh would agree with me.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But to have the input and perspective from patient groups, from consumers, certainly, that would be something that could be taken as part of the process.
